authority: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW)
interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: The Ministry's current Shipping Guidelines index and the component-specific SbDS/SBFAS guidelines are primary. Greenfield cluster, brownfield expansion, risk coverage and vessel-contract assistance remain separate records because they have different beneficiaries, application routes and benefit mechanics. UdyamVeda prepares evidence but does not certify DPRs, domestic content, insurance coverage or Government approvals.

supportingSources.anchor: Official Ministry page for Greenfield Shipbuilding Cluster Development under SbDS
Official Ministry guidelines index listing current Greenfield, Brownfield and Risk Coverage guidelines

records.sourceAnchor: SPV/State-Centre or Central-entity route, eligible shared cluster infrastructure, DPR, approval, capital assistance and monitoring
observations: The record is an institutional greenfield shipbuilding-cluster route, not an ordinary standalone startup or shipyard grant.

The seed distinguishes eligible SPV/Central-entity structures, anchor shipyard responsibilities, common maritime/landside infrastructure, DPR and National Shipbuilding Mission/implementation-agency approvals.

The Ministry guideline and seed preserve a validity boundary for applications approved from 24 September 2025 through 31 March 2036, but that period does not establish a live project intake or guarantee sanction.

Capital assistance is limited to eligible items and is conditional on approval, KPIs, climate resilience, insurance, utilization and quarterly reporting; scheme-level or cluster-level amounts are not an individual company entitlement.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current SPV composition, eligible location, State/Centre contribution, anchor-shipyard role and implementation agency.
Confirm the current DPR format, eligible-item schedule, capital-assistance rate, sanction authority, tranche rules and budget availability.
Check KPI, environmental, climate-resilience, insurance, procurement, utilization and quarterly-reporting obligations.
Obtain an authorized reviewer decision before presenting this route to a private business or publishing any amount.

supportingSources.anchor: Official Ministry page for Brownfield Capacity Expansion under SbDS
Official Ministry guidelines index and publication dates

records.sourceAnchor: Existing Indian shipyard, three-year operating-history condition, 25% approved project-cost grant, financial closure and four tranches
observations: The Brownfield record is for an existing Indian shipyard expanding or modernizing eligible shipbuilding/repair capacity; it is separate from greenfield cluster development.

The seed captures the 25% approved-project-cost boundary, an implementation overview cap of up to Rs 1,500 crore per shipyard, four tranche percentages and the requirement for complete financial closure before the first tranche.
The validity boundary through 31 March 2036 is a scheme approval boundary, not proof that every shipyard can apply or that funds are available without appraisal.
The grant is conditional on Schedule I eligibility, DPR approval, monitoring, utilization, milestone and completion certification; the cap and grant rate are not automatic sanction.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the three-year operating-history test, Indian entity status, Schedule I eligible costs and current project-intake route.
Confirm approved project cost, cap, grant calculation, financial-closure evidence and 15/30/35/20 tranche triggers.
Check IA/NSbM appraisal, third-party monitoring, utilization certificates, completion certificate and recovery/adjustment conditions.
Obtain an authorized reviewer decision before displaying a grant estimate or treating the route as actionable.

supportingSources.anchor: Official Ministry page for SbDS Shipbuilding Risk Coverage
Official risk-coverage guideline: validity, nominated agencies and coverage types

records.sourceAnchor: Pre-shipment, post-shipment and vendor-default risk coverage, nominated Credit Risk Cover Agencies and Sagarmala implementation route
observations: The Risk Coverage record is an insurance/risk-mitigation route, not a direct grant, loan, equity investment or unconditional Government guarantee.
The guideline identifies pre-shipment, post-shipment and vendor-default risks and states that Government-nominated Credit Risk Cover Agencies design/administer the relevant products.
The seed identifies Sagarmala Financial Corporation Limited as implementation agency and preserves the 24 September 2025 to 31 March 2036 validity boundary.

Coverage depends on a live approved product, policy wording, premium, deductible, exclusions, security, claim process and project/contract terms; qualifying for another SbDS component does not create automatic coverage.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the currently nominated Credit Risk Cover Agency, live product, policy wording, premium, deductible, exclusions and limits.
Classify the exposure as pre-shipment, post-shipment or vendor default and confirm the eligible contract/project and insured party.
Check underwriting, security, claim, audit, reporting and implementation-agency documents before recommending.
Keep risk coverage separate from grants, loans and revenue protection; obtain an authorized reviewer decision.

supportingSources.anchor: Official Ministry page for modified SBFAS guidelines
Official current guidelines index: SBFAS modified 7 January 2026

records.sourceAnchor: Qualifying vessel contracts, 45-day application, domestic-content threshold, vessel-category rates, price basis, milestones and final verification
observations: The modified SBFAS guideline dated 7 January 2026 provides a vessel-contract financial-assistance route for eligible Indian shipyards, separate from SbDS cluster and risk-coverage records.

The seed captures the 45-day application deadline after signing the qualifying contract, domestic-content treatment below 30%, from 30% to below 40%, and at least 40%, and the vessel-category assistance rates.

The financial assistance is calculated using the prescribed contract/fair-price and actual-payment rules and is conditional on India-based construction, domestic-content evidence, verification, milestones and delivery; the rate is not a guaranteed cash amount.

The current guideline index shows the SBFAS publication separately from amended SBFAP material, so transition treatment, Schedule I exclusions and any interaction with earlier policy must be reconciled per contract.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the live SBFAS portal, contract date, vessel category, Schedule I exclusions and any SBFAP/SBFAS transition treatment.
Confirm domestic-content formula, Chartered Accountant certification, fair-price basis, 45-day deadline, application number and competent-authority route.
Check construction, commissioning, trial, payment, delivery, security, inspection, audit, tranche and final re-evaluation requirements.
Keep SBFAS separate from logistics, shipping-company operations, loans and SbDS benefits; obtain a reviewer decision before calculating support.

publicationGuard.reason: Official MoPSW pages and component guidelines confirm four distinct shipbuilding routes, but current intake, project/contract-specific eligibility, implementing-agency capacity, live risk products, transition rules and reviewer decisions remain unresolved. All records stay human-review pending.
